prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Design Your Desktop Companion", "Select traits and preview your pet live before finalizing adoption.", "Live Companion Preview"]
1: ["Mastering Your Desktop Companion", "Right-click your pet anytime to access quick settings, talk, or minimize to system tray.", "Desktop Control Guide", "Got It, Let's Go!"]
2: ["Your Companion Journey Begins", "Discover how desktop pets interact with your workspace and pick your path."]
3: []
4: ["Signing in secures your pet traits so your companion follows you on any device."]
5: ["Generating Your Desktop Pet...", "We are preparing high-res animations and desktop collision scripts."]
6: ["Includes exclusive Starter Crown accessory badge!", "Starter Accessory Unlocked"]
7: []
8: ["We'll ping you when your desktop companion is ready to pop up!"]
9: ["Your Companion is Live on Your Desktop!", "Drag your pet anywhere on your screen. Access settings anytime via system tray icon."]

verdicts.problem: Mentions exclusive starter accessory badge, creating scarcity or highlighting free extras.
